contract: EF Core 10 relational runtime and design-time public API conformance
providerFamily: relational runtime with EF design-time API inventory
inventoryRule: A public API entry without an explicit disposition or linked behavioral test remains uncovered; inventory presence alone does not imply conformance.
capabilityRule: Capability declarations control applicability only and never modify expected results.

dispositionRules.reason: These are public query provider service and expression APIs. The suite does not invoke provider services directly; it verifies translation and results through public IQueryable operations.

These are public storage and type-mapping service APIs used by provider implementations. Their observable mapping behavior is exercised through persistence and type-fidelity tests rather than direct service calls.
These are public update pipeline service APIs used by provider implementations. Persistence behavior is tested through DbContext SaveChanges and other public application operations.
These are EF Core design-time and code-generation APIs; they do not define relational provider runtime behavior.
Diagnostic identifiers, event payloads, and logging helpers are owned by EF Core. Provider-observable interception behavior is covered through public SaveChanges tests where applicable.

These are EF Core fluent model-configuration APIs. Provider obligations concern the observable effect of the configured model, which is tested through schema, query, migration, and persistence behavior rather than each builder overload in isolation.
Model convention execution and convention set construction are owned by EF Core. Provider behavior is checked through the finalized model's observable schema and query behavior.
These are convention-time model metadata interfaces and extension points. This black-box suite does not invoke provider convention services directly.
Mutable model metadata APIs define EF Core model construction behavior. Providers are assessed by honoring the resulting model through public database operations.
Read-only model metadata APIs are owned by EF Core and are independent of relational provider execution behavior.
Runtime metadata implementation types are EF Core model infrastructure, not provider-specific public behavior.
These EF Core relational fluent APIs configure model metadata. Provider conformance is evaluated through observable behavior of models configured with those APIs.
These APIs inspect relational model metadata owned by EF Core. This suite does not test provider implementation details by inspecting metadata extensions.
These APIs inspect relational property metadata owned by EF Core. Provider mapping behavior is assessed through persistence and value-fidelity results.
These EF Core relational fluent APIs configure property metadata. Provider effects are evaluated through public queries, schema creation, migrations, and persistence.
These EF Core relational fluent APIs configure model metadata. Provider effects are evaluated through public database behavior.
These APIs inspect EF Core relational model metadata. The black-box contract checks resulting database behavior rather than metadata internals.
These APIs inspect EF Core relational type metadata. Provider behavior is checked through schema, query, and persistence results.
These EF Core model-building overloads configure primitive collection metadata; collection persistence and query results are the provider contract tested here.
These EF Core model-building overloads configure complex property metadata; provider obligations are assessed through complex value persistence and query behavior.
These EF Core model-building overloads configure complex primitive collection metadata; provider obligations are assessed through observable persistence and query behavior.
Relational annotation name constants are EF Core metadata identifiers and do not define provider runtime behavior.
This is an EF Core options service-extension implementation surface. The suite configures providers through public DbContextOptionsBuilder APIs and verifies resulting behavior.
This is an EF Core relational service-extension implementation surface. The suite configures providers through public options APIs and verifies resulting behavior.
This type maps EF Core internal service registrations and is outside the black-box provider boundary.

These are EF Core model metadata APIs. Provider conformance is checked through the configured model's observable schema, query, migration, and persistence behavior instead of direct metadata inspection.
These are design-time reverse-engineering APIs. They are outside the relational runtime provider contract tested by this suite.
Change tracking entry and collection APIs are owned by EF Core. Provider interaction is covered through tests that load, modify, and persist entities via public APIs.
Generic options builder behavior is owned by EF Core. Provider configuration is supplied through the adapter and its resulting runtime behavior is tested.
ModelBuilder behavior is owned by EF Core. Provider obligations are tested against the built model through schema, query, migration, and persistence outcomes.
Pre-convention model configuration is owned by EF Core; provider effects are evaluated through the resulting model's observable database behavior.
Execution strategy behavior is provider-specific and explicitly outside the base relational conformance contract.
Migration operation objects are inputs to EF Core's provider migration services, not app-facing operations. Observable support is evaluated through applying migrations.
Migration history repository types are provider service APIs. The suite checks applied and pending migration state through public DatabaseFacade APIs.
Migration annotation provider types are provider service APIs and are not invoked directly by the black-box suite.
Relational annotation name constants are EF Core metadata identifiers and do not define provider runtime behavior.
Relational annotation name constants are EF Core metadata identifiers and do not define provider runtime behavior.
These extensions inspect relational index metadata. Provider index behavior is checked through observable schema and migration behavior.
These extensions inspect relational foreign-key metadata. Provider relationship behavior is checked through persistence and navigation operations.
These extensions inspect relational key metadata. Provider key behavior is checked through persistence and generated-value scenarios.
These extensions inspect relational trigger metadata. Trigger metadata is outside this suite's baseline provider behavior contract.
These extensions inspect relational primitive collection element metadata. Provider collection behavior is checked through persistence and query results.

This public infrastructure namespace contains EF-owned model/runtime helpers and provider service extension points. The suite tests application-facing context, connection, factory, and interception behavior through their public results; it does not inspect provider services or EF implementation helpers.

Value-generator classes and selector services are provider implementation extension points. The suite checks generated values through public entity persistence and retrieval instead of invoking provider generators directly.
Provider-specific options are configured by the adapter. Shared tests evaluate the resulting public EF Core behavior without depending on provider-specific option-builder implementations.

These generic dependency-injection registration methods are owned by EF Core. The suite checks provider use through scoped contexts and context factories; provider pooling implementation details are outside this contract.

Logger category names and nested category helpers are EF Core diagnostics identifiers. Provider behavior is checked through public operation results and interception callbacks, not SQL logging output.
EventSource instrumentation is EF Core runtime diagnostics and is not a provider API contract.
EF Core metrics payload helpers are runtime diagnostics, not provider-observable database behavior.
This method returns generated SQL text. SQL inspection is explicitly outside the black-box conformance boundary.
Query tags are observable through generated command text only and do not change the logical query result. SQL-text assertions are outside this suite's boundary.
Call-site query tags are observable through generated command text only and do not change the logical query result. SQL-text assertions are outside this suite's boundary.
Provider-specific execution strategy behavior is explicitly outside the baseline relational provider contract.
Context identity values and their equality/formatting are assigned by EF Core and do not exercise provider behavior.
This property exposes EF model metadata. The suite evaluates the configured entity model through database operations rather than inspecting model internals.
Exception construction is owned by EF Core. Provider-raised write failures and their affected entity entries are tested through SaveChanges.
Exception construction is owned by EF Core. Provider concurrency behavior is tested through conflicting persistence operations and resolution.
FromExpression constructs query roots for application-defined queryable functions. Its expression-root construction is EF-owned; provider translation is tested through ordinary query execution.

This interface is a provider migration-history service. Applied/pending migration behavior and history persistence are tested through the public DatabaseFacade migration APIs, without resolving provider services.
This interface is a provider migration service used to interpret model annotations. Migration behavior is checked by applying public migration classes, not by invoking provider services directly.
These constructor dependencies belong to the provider migration SQL-generation service and are excluded by the black-box boundary.
This builder is part of provider SQL-generation infrastructure. The suite validates migrations by applying them and observing schema/data behavior, without inspecting generated SQL commands.
SQL generation is a provider implementation service. Conformance is tested by applying migrations through DatabaseFacade and observing the resulting database behavior.
Migration command objects are provider service output and expose implementation details excluded from this black-box suite.
Migration execution state is an EF/provider implementation detail. The suite checks externally visible migration state through applied and pending migration APIs.
This interface exposes migration assembly services. The suite tests migration discovery through the public DatabaseFacade APIs instead of resolving provider or EF services.
Command executor services are provider implementation infrastructure; migrations are verified through public migration operations and database results.
The service interface is an implementation entry point. The app-facing migration contract is exercised through Database.Migrate and Database.MigrateAsync.
Migration locking is provider execution infrastructure. This suite does not inspect transaction or lock implementations; it verifies migration outcomes through public APIs.
Model differ services are design/runtime infrastructure. The suite does not generate provider migration operations from model metadata.
This interface is a provider SQL-generation service. Generated SQL is outside the black-box contract; migrations are tested through apply/rollback results.
Migration ID generation is EF tooling/runtime infrastructure. The suite supplies fixed migration IDs and tests their discovery and application.
These helpers operate on the migrations service; migration discovery is tested through public DatabaseFacade methods.
These are EF Core model-creation service dependencies. The suite tests the resulting configured model through public database operations rather than constructing or inspecting services.
This method returns generated SQL text, which is explicitly excluded from the black-box conformance boundary.

Options extension enumeration and mutation expose provider configuration and service-extension objects. The suite configures providers through the adapter and checks behavior through ordinary DbContext operations.
Formatting a context does not exercise provider behavior.
Context object equality is owned by EF Core and does not exercise provider behavior.
Context hashing is owned by EF Core and does not exercise provider behavior.
The context-to-facade accessor is owned by EF Core. DatabaseFacade operations are tested through their public observable behavior.
The context-to-tracker accessor is owned by EF Core. Provider interaction is tested through tracked persistence and query results.
This accessor exposes EF model metadata. Direct model metadata inspection is outside the black-box provider boundary; the suite validates the model through its database behavior.
Context identity is assigned by EF Core and does not depend on provider behavior.
DbContext construction is owned by EF Core. The suite verifies configured provider use through actual operations on constructed contexts.
This API is covered by the sync connection lifecycle contract; test coverage takes precedence over this fallback disposition.
This API is covered by the async connection lifecycle contract; test coverage takes precedence over this fallback disposition.

This formats EF Core's public debug view. Provider conformance is measured through database-visible operations and results, not formatting diagnostics.
This formats EF Core model metadata for diagnostics. It does not perform or define provider database behavior.
This operates on EF Core query expression tree structures. The suite verifies query translation through application LINQ results and does not call expression transformation helpers directly.
This adapts in-memory collections for data binding and does not interact with a database provider.
History rows are the persistence representation used by provider migration-history services. Migration lifecycle behavior is tested through DatabaseFacade APIs and applied database state.
This enum configures provider migration-lock lifecycle behavior. Lock implementation details are outside the black-box contract; migration outcomes are verified through public APIs.
These flags configure generated migration scripts and transaction text. Generated SQL inspection and SQL-script formatting are outside this runtime database-behavior suite.
The constructor creates an EF Core event payload. Provider failure behavior is tested by causing and observing SaveChanges failures through the public API.
The constructor creates an EF Core event payload. Provider save behavior is tested through SaveChanges and the emitted public event.
The constructor creates an EF Core event payload. Provider save behavior is tested through SaveChanges and the emitted public event.
This flag marks EF Core design-time model construction and does not represent a runtime relational provider operation.

This public constructor initializes EF Core's migration operation builder. Provider conformance is exercised by applying operations through DatabaseFacade migration APIs and verifying resulting database state.

This property exposes the in-memory operations accumulated by EF Core's migration builder. Inspecting that list would test EF Core's migration construction internals rather than provider-visible behavior.

Database sequences are an optional native database feature. Test sequence creation and use only for providers declaring the sequences capability; current SQLite and MySQL profiles do not declare support.
Sequence alteration applies only where the database supports sequences. Test its observable migration effect for providers declaring the sequences capability.
Sequence removal applies only where the database supports sequences. Test its observable migration effect for providers declaring the sequences capability.
Sequence rename applies only where the database supports sequences and sequence renames. Test resulting sequence behavior for providers declaring the relevant capability.
Sequence restart applies only where the database supports sequences. Test generated value behavior after restart for providers declaring the sequences capability.
Schema creation is database-specific. Test it only where the provider declares schema support and verify the resulting namespace through public database behavior.
Schema removal is database-specific. Test it only where the provider declares schema support and verify resulting object availability through public database behavior.
Database-wide collation and other database options vary by database engine. Test migration effects only for providers declaring database-collation-migration support.
Schema-qualified function names depend on database namespace and function support. Exercise the configured function through LINQ only for providers declaring schema-qualified-functions support.
